title: Mirror edges improved prediction between two adult worm maps after physical contact controls
abstract: We tested whether a left-right mirror connection predicts chemical edge presence in a second C. elegans map after control for measured physical contact. We used Witvliet maps 8 and 7 for adults, and maps 1 and 2 for an L1 age check. In 1703 selected adult edges, the mirror marker improved the source-family held-out log score by 0.02745 nats per edge after contact controls. A nominal two-way family bootstrap interval was 0.00630 to 0.04883. The adult target-family gain was 0.02615. The L1 source-family gains were 0.06527 and 0.03592; the interval for the second gain included zero. Only one adult direction had a contact matrix. The maps came from four different animals; the L1 animals had different ages. The test measures observed wiring reproducibility, not reliable neural activity or a causal effect of symmetry. The package provides new code, aggregate scores, a figure, and exact retrieval and regeneration instructions. External data and record-level tables are not bundled.

display.caption: Mirror score gains before and after physical contact controls. Bars show nominal 95 percent two-way family bootstrap intervals with fitted predictions fixed. L1 maps 1 and 2 have ages 0 and 5 hours. The two holdout tests reuse the same edges.
